questions.question: The shortest path algorithm for nonnegative edge lengths $\ell_{uv}$ starts with $d(s)=0$ and settled set $U=\{s\}$, and repeatedly adds one vertex to $U$. At each step it looks at edges $u-v$ with $u\in U$ and $v\notin U$. Which quantity does the chosen edge minimize?
options: $d(u)+\ell_{uv}$, the full route length to $v$ via $u$
$\ell_{uv}$, the length of the connecting edge on its own
$d(u)$, the label of the settled end of the edge
$\ell_{uv}$ over edges leaving the vertex most recently added

questions.question: The shortest path algorithm for nonnegative edge lengths $\ell_{uv}$ starts with $d(s)=0$ and settled set $U=\{s\}$, and repeatedly adds one vertex to $U$. In which order do vertices enter $U$?
options: In order of the number of edges on a route from the origin
In the order in which an edge to them is first examined
In order of the shortest single edge leading into them
In order of their shortest route length from the origin

questions.question: The shortest path algorithm for nonnegative edge lengths $\ell_{uv}$ starts with $d(s)=0$ and settled set $U=\{s\}$, and repeatedly adds one vertex to $U$. At some step two candidate edges give the same smallest value of $d(u)+\ell_{uv}$. What should be done if one shortest path is enough?
options: Choose the edge with the smaller length $\ell_{uv}$.
Choose either edge; ties may be broken arbitrarily.
Restart the algorithm with one of the edges removed.
Stop, since no unique shortest path exists then.

questions.question: The shortest path algorithm for nonnegative edge lengths $\ell_{uv}$ starts with $d(s)=0$ and settled set $U=\{s\}$, and repeatedly adds one vertex to $U$. Instead of stopping at a destination, it is continued until no further vertex can be added. What do the final labels $d(v)$ give?
options: The shortest distance between every pair of vertices
Distances between any two vertices as label differences
Distances only for the vertices on one route from $s$
The shortest distance from $s$ to each reached vertex

questions.question: An undirected network has edge lengths S–A 4, S–B 1, B–A 2, A–T 5 and B–T 8. The shortest path algorithm is run from origin S (with $d(S)=0$, settled set $U=\{S\}$). Which vertex is added to $U$ first, and with which label?
options: B, with label 1
A, with label 4
A, with label 3
B, with label 2

questions.question: On an undirected network with edges S–A (4), S–B (1), B–A (2), A–T (5) and B–T (8), the shortest path algorithm from S has just settled B with $d(B)=1$. Which vertex does it settle next, and with which label?
options: A, with label 4
A, with label 2
A, with label 3
T, with label 9

questions.question: A run of the shortest path algorithm from S gives labels $d(B)=1$, $d(A)=2$, $d(C)=4$, $d(D)=6$, $d(T)=7$ and predecessors pred(B) = S, pred(A) = S, pred(C) = A, pred(D) = C, pred(T) = C. Which route from S to T does it give?
options: S, A, C, D, T
S, A, C, T
S, B, A, C, D, T
S, B, C, T

questions.question: The shortest path algorithm for nonnegative edge lengths $\ell_{uv}$ starts with $d(s)=0$ and settled set $U=\{s\}$, and repeatedly adds one vertex to $U$. For a single destination $t$, why may the run stop as soon as $t$ is added to $U$?
options: Once some edge to $t$ is seen, its value is final.
The run may stop only when every vertex is in $U$.
Once $t$ is in $U$, its label $d(t)$ no longer changes.
The run may stop once all edges at $t$ have been examined.

questions.question: The shortest path algorithm for nonnegative edge lengths $\ell_{uv}$ starts with $d(s)=0$ and settled set $U=\{s\}$, and repeatedly adds one vertex to $U$. Why does each step consider only edges $u-v$ with $u\in U$ and $v\notin U$?
options: Edges inside $U$ are used later to shorten labels in $U$
Edges with both ends outside $U$ would give labels too small
Any edge may be chosen; the restriction only saves effort
$d(u)$ is known only for $u\in U$; each $v\in U$ is settled

questions.question: An undirected network has edge lengths S–A 4, S–B 2, B–A 1, A–C 5, B–C 9, B–D 9, C–D 2, C–T 6 and D–T 3. Running the shortest path algorithm from S, what label $d(T)$ does T receive?

An undirected network has these edges, listed by end vertex. From S: A 4, B 2. From B: A 1, C 9, D 9. From C: A 5, D 2, T 6. From D: T 3. Its shortest S-to-T route has length 13. If C–D is lengthened from 2 to 6, what label $d(T)$ does the shortest path algorithm from S give?
The shortest path algorithm is run from S on an undirected network with lengths S–A 2, S–B 3 and B–A $-2$, although it is stated for nonnegative lengths. What goes wrong?
options: Nothing; the labels are still the shortest distances.
B gets label 3, though route S–A–B has length 0.
The algorithm cannot start because of the negative length.
A gets label 2, though route S–B–A has length 1.

questions.question: The shortest path algorithm for nonnegative edge lengths $\ell_{uv}$ starts with $d(s)=0$ and settled set $U=\{s\}$, and repeatedly adds one vertex to $U$. Vertex $v$ is added with predecessor $u$. Must every shortest route from $s$ to $v$ pass through $u$?
options: Yes; the predecessor lies on each shortest route.
Yes, if the edge $u-v$ is the shortest edge at $v$.
No; a shortest route never uses the predecessor.
No; with ties another shortest route may avoid $u$.

questions.question: A shortest path algorithm run from S gives $d(A)=3$, $d(B)=5$ and $d(C)=9$, with predecessor pred(C) = B. The network also has an edge A–C. Which statement about its length $\ell_{AC}$ must be true?
options: $\ell_{AC}\ge 6$
$\ell_{AC}\ge 9$
$\ell_{AC}\le 6$

questions.question: An undirected network has lengths S–A 2, S–B 7, A–T 3, A–C 1, C–D 4 and B–T 1. The shortest path algorithm from S stops as soon as T is added. Which vertices are still outside $U$ then?
options: B and D
D only
B, C and D
None of them

questions.question: In a run of the shortest path algorithm from S, $U=\{S,A\}$ with $d(S)=0$ and $d(A)=4$. The edges from $U$ to unsettled vertices are S–B (length 5), A–C (length 2) and A–B (length 3). Which vertex is added next, and with which label?
options: C, with label 6 via A–C
C, with label 2 via A–C
B, with label 5 via S–B
B, with label 7 via A–B
